To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tetrasubsititutional site on the argon matrix plane is likely to be the most stable site for formic acid dimers, and the calculated IR spectra are in agreement with experimental data.
the supermolecule approach is capable of modeling matrix-isolated molecules and that it can be applied to simulate their vibrational spectra.
the matrix-isolated FAD is stable in the tetrasubstituted Ar(111) site.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an efficient method for modeling and simulating matrix-isolated molecules, which is applicable to the study of a wide range of systems, including those that cannot be treated with conventional cluster models.
the development of a theoretical approach for modeling matrix-isolated molecules, which is based on the density functional method and the supermolecule approach.
the modeling and spectral simulation of molecules embedded in solid matrices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for FAD in solid Ar, the most stable structure is the tetrasubstituted one, in which FAD is located on Ar(111), with the C-H bonds pointing towards the matrix surface.
the supermolecule approach is able to predict with reasonable accuracy the structural stability and the spectral features of the matrix-isolated species.
, in general, matrix-isolated molecules are modeled by means of supermolecule calculations, and that the results obtained are consistent with the experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the supermolecule approach is capable of reproducing the spectral features of FAD in argon matrix, in particular the red-shifts of the ν(OH) stretching and ν(C=O) bending modes, and also the splitting of the ν(CO) stretching mode.

the matrix-isolation model based on the supermolecule approach is a promising tool for modeling matrix-embedded molecules, and the spectral simulation is a useful tool in the interpretation of the experimental spectra.

the matrix-isolated FAD can be modeled as a supermolecule in which the FAD molecule is embedded in the first solvatation shell of 26 argon atoms and that the calculated spectra for FAD-Ar(26) are in good agreement with experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supermolecule approach can be successfully applied to model matrix-isolated molecules, provided that the host atom is sufficiently large and the guest atom(s) is/are not strongly polarizable.
the spectral simulations of matrix-isolated systems are possible by combining the density functional calculations and the supermolecule approach.

the supermolecule approach can provide reliable information on the structural stability and simulated spectra for matrix-isolated molecules, provided that the host-guest interaction is properly evaluated.
